derivation.device: adiabatic 1x2 mode-evolution power splitter (from Phase-A classification)

how_the_FoM_is_governed.split_balance: Structural: the geometry is mirror-symmetric about the axis, so the input fundamental excites only the SYMMETRIC supermode, which by symmetry deposits equal power in the two outer guides. 50/50 is guaranteed by construction, independent of platform. Predict 0.500.
how_the_FoM_is_governed.transmission_total: Adiabaticity + bend loss. Power stays in the fundamental supermode iff the taper evolves slowly vs the local supermode beat length L_beat = lambda/(2*dn); the bottleneck is the phase-match point (minimum dn). Radiation at the fan-out adds loss unless the S-bend radius >= min_bend_radius.

what_must_change_with_platform_and_why: 1) Guide widths -> single_mode_width_um (rule-based): center_input = arm_width = wg; all tips = min_feature. Wider, less-confined platforms need wider single-mode guides.

2) Coupling gap -> min_feature (strongest fab-allowed coupling => shortest adiabatic length). arm_offset = wg/2 + coupling_gap. With COMPLEMENTARY linear tapers (center wg->tip, outer tip->wg) the two widths sum to ~const, so center-outer edge gap stays ~= coupling_gap through the whole transfer and phase-match sits at w = wg/2.

3) Transfer (taper) length -> set from the LOCAL supermode coupling length at phase-match L_c = lambda/(2*dn) at (w=wg/2, gap=min_feature). Adiabaticity needs L_taper >~ a few x L_c. This is the platform-dependent scaling and is COMPUTED from mode solves, not guessed.
4) Fan-out S-bend -> sized so effective radius R_eff = 2*L^2/(pi^2*dy) >= min_bend_radius (bend radiation also cuts T).
5) Footprint kept within the per-stack budget (which scales with confinement).

iterations.reasoning: Strong confinement: phase-match L_c=7.96um. taper=38um = 4.8x L_c => deeply adiabatic. Fan-out R_eff=2*12^2/(pi^2*2.57)=11.4um >= min_bend_radius 5um. Balance structural. Predict T~0.98.

Round-1 diagnosis: my complementary tapers with both tips=mf make widths sum to (wg+mf), so the TRUE phase-match gap was mf/2 (0.09um) -> MERGED Y-junction regime; transfer was already 13x adiabatic, so the 7% loss was the center pinch-off tip radiating, not transfer. Fix: arm_offset=wg/2+1.5mf makes the gap a constant mf=0.18um (unmerged evanescent coupler), still 8x adiabatic (Lc=4.97um). Sine (C1-continuous) fan-out removes the raised-cosine curvature jump. Predict T~0.97.
iterations.fixture_issue: Round-2 shortened input_straight 2->1um; the FDTD source at x=0.5um sat ~0.5um from both the left PML and the taper start (x=1) -> corrupt input normalization (T>1). Device geometry is valid; fixture needs a clean input-access stub.

iterations.change: DEVICE unchanged from round 2 (its geometry is valid). FIXTURE fixed: 8um input-access straight so the source sits 5um from the taper and 4um from the PML; input port [-4,0]; output ports [64,+/-3.0] on 8um isolated stubs, 9um past the S-bend end (x=56).
iterations.reasoning: Round-2 device is an 8x-adiabatic unmerged (gap=mf) evanescent coupler with a C1 fan-out; the invalid reading was purely the fixture source placement. With a clean input access, predict T~0.97.
iterations.result: REGRESSION vs round-1 on BOTH axes (T 0.928->0.880, balance 0.500->0.4638).

final.best_device: round-1 geometry (restored as the committed device_soi220.py/gds)
final.note: soi220's honest best is round 1: T=0.928 (miss by 0.022), balance 0.500 exact PASS. Physics lesson: the unmerge fix (gap mf/2 -> mf) that CLOSED sin400 REGRESSED soi220 (round-3 T=0.880, balance 0.4638). On strong-confinement SOI the tighter merged-regime coupling is cleaner; opening the gap both lowered T and (via the wider, sine-fanned outputs) broke the exact 50/50 balance. Retargeting is not one-size-fits-all across confinement regimes. Committed device = round-1 best.
